text:
lauren: Quick thought 1: should we move the console permissions surface to a stitched GraphQL gateway instead of the current REST mesh? want to weigh caching, telemetry, and rollout UX tradeoffs.

ben: quick take: graphql helps the client fetch exactly what it needs which is nice for perf, but stitching adds coupling and makes cache semantics fuzzy.

seema: big worry is invalidation for the effective-permissions card. today we do TTL + pubsub invalidation on role-binding changes. with stitched resolvers we could get partial cached fields that are painful to clear.

tom: can you sketch what a stitched query might look like?

ben: example:
```
query EffectivePermissions($tenant: ID!, $route: String!, $user: ID!) {
  tenant(id: $tenant) {
    id
    effectiveRoles(user: $user) {
      id
      name
      scopes
      source { id sourceType }
    }
    routePermissions(route: $route) {
      allowed
      quotaUsed
      quotaLimit
      overrides { source expiresAt }
    }
  }
}
```

lauren: that looks good. the console needs both a compact preview and a heavy audit table. graphql reduces overfetch, but we must keep telemetry consistent between views.

seema: telemetry detail: currently our REST calls attach tags: route, role-hash, env. with a gateway we risk losing which upstream service fulfilled a field unless the gateway emits resolver-level spans and labels. we should require resolver metadata.

kate: rollout UX: if we flip console to the gateway for a canary cohort, users may see temporarily stale entitlements depending on cache settings. we need a safe fallback to REST per-user in case of mismatch.

ben: proposed implementation plan:
1) add resolver-level span tags (service, resolverName, cacheHit boolean)
2) gateway sets X-Resolved-By headers when in debug mode
3) console feature-flag per user to toggle gql vs rest
4) auth-service emits strict invalidation events; add subscriber in gateway
5) internal canary: 5% infra/devs, then 25% orgs, monitor errors

seva: on invalidation hooks: can infra guarantee pubsub delivery under 30s? if not we should show "last-evaluated" timestamps in the UI to signal potential staleness.

tom: quotas: routePermissions returns quota fields but enforcement stays in infra/dedicated. i suggest we only display telemetry-based usage; do not rely on gateway aggregation for enforcement.

lauren: agreed. display-only is safer. console reads quotaUsed/limit from telemetry API; enforcement remains upstream.

seema: audit logs: if a resolver composes roles from multiple sources, the audit entry must list all contributing sources with IDs and change timestamps, so compliance can parse programmatically.

kate: UX edge-case: pending approvals. the permissions preview should show queued/dashed state when a binding is awaiting approval. graphql can return a small status enum but UI needs deterministic mapping for states.

ben: implementation note: avoid deeply nested stitched types for frequently-read fields. flatten hot-paths (effectiveRolesList) and keep heavy audit tables as separately paginated endpoints.

lauren: next steps: ben + seva prototype gateway headers + spans, seema draft audit shape for security review, kate add console feature-flag and queued-state mapping, tom confirm quota display source. i'll draft a 1-pager for security and oncall with sample traces.

seema: tagging teams: @security please review resolver-level telemetry and audit shape. @infra can we commit to pubsub invalidation SLA?

audit-bot: NOTE: security review requested (ticket INF-4231). assigned: security-team. ETA 48h.

deploy-bot: calendar event created: "RBAC Gateway Rollout sync" tomorrow 11:00 (30m).

lauren: thanks all :thumbsup: 

ben: i'll post a prototype trace snippet and a minimal gateway headers patch in this thread once ready.

kate: ui question: per-field loading skeletons or single global loader for effective-permissions? my vote: per-field, so panels populate progressively. less jarring.

tom: per-field + show authoritative "last-evaluated at" timestamp for each block so users can see staleness surface.

lauren: agreed. sync tomorrow 11am to finalize canary cohorts and acceptance criteria.

seema: added: acceptance criteria idea -> resolver-level spans present in traces, audit event includes source list, invalidation events processed within 30s for >95% of cases, console feature-flag available.

ben: i'll prototype and push a small PoC branch with gateway header + span tags. will add a README showing how to interpret spans.

lauren: perfect. thanks everyone.
